The digital lending operating model: RE, LSP and DLA

After this lesson you can:
  • Describe the RE–LSP–DLA triangle created by the Digital Lending Directions
  • Explain DLA reporting and why app inventories exist
  • State the conduct rules that follow an LSP everywhere

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Three actors, one accountability line
  2. Conduct duties that never switch off
  3. How LoanOS holds the triangle
  4. Regulatory anchors

  6. Knowledge check

1. Three actors, one accountability line

Modern Indian lending is rarely the RE alone. The Digital Lending Directions define the operating model:

  • The RE holds the licence, the credit risk and the accountability.
  • An LSP (Lending Service Provider) acts for the RE — sourcing, servicing, support, collections — under a contract and due diligence.
  • A DLA (Digital Lending App or website) is the borrower-facing surface, owned by the RE or by an LSP.

Every DLA an RE uses — its own and its LSPs' — must be reported to the RBI through CIMS, with public disclosures kept current. An unreported app through which loans flow is a direct violation.

2. Conduct duties that never switch off

The directions attach conduct rules to this triangle that a BA will meet repeatedly in this course:

  • Borrowers must know they are dealing with the RE: identity, charges and grievance paths are disclosed up front.
  • An LSP presenting offers from multiple lenders must present them neutrally — complete, comparable, no dark patterns.
  • Fees to the LSP are paid by the RE, not smuggled into borrower charges.
  • Funds never sit in or pass through LSP-controlled accounts (module 4 covers the fund-flow rule in depth).
  • Data collected by a DLA is need-based, consented and India-resident.

3. How LoanOS holds the triangle

LoanOS keeps three registries the RE governs: the LSP registry (agreement, enhanced due diligence, periodic review, borrower-facing disclosures, RE-paid fee controls), the DLA registry (ownership, grievance contact, RE website linkage, CIMS-ready export rows, CCO attestation) and the channel-conduct evidence trail that attributes every partner action. Channel users can source and service within their scope, but they cannot approve credit or promise outcomes — authority stays with the RE's staff and policies.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-DL-2025 — Defines the RE/LSP/DLA model, disclosure, neutrality and conduct duties.
  • RBI-DLA-CIMS — Own and LSP DLAs must be reported on RBI CIMS with public disclosures.
  • CCPA-DARK-PATTERNS — Multi-lender offer views must avoid deceptive patterns; ranking must be explained.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability PAR-001 — LSP agreement, role, due diligence, review, data and fee controls.
  • Capability RPT-002 — DLA CIMS export and CCO certification.
  • Capability CHN-010 — Channel conduct, consent and disclosure monitoring.
  • Capability OFR-003 — Objective ranking disclosure and dark-pattern prevention in offer views.

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Which DLAs must an RE report to RBI CIMS?

  1. Only apps the RE owns
  2. Only apps that disburse loans
  3. Its own DLAs and those of its LSPs
  4. Only Android apps
Reveal answer and reasoning

C. The reporting duty covers every digital lending surface used in the RE's lending — RE-owned and LSP-owned alike.

2. An LSP marketplace shows offers from four REs but hides one lender's higher processing fee behind a tap. What rule does this break?

  1. Fund-flow
  2. Offer neutrality / dark-pattern prevention
  3. KYC
  4. Data residency
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Multi-lender presentation must be complete and comparable; obscuring cost information is a dark pattern the directions prohibit.
